one_liner: BigCommerce offers a broad REST and GraphQL API. Free sandbox/trial stores give working API credentials, and the vendor has official MCP servers (Storefront, Store Management, WebMCP, Docs).
auth_notes: Store-level API accounts give a static access token sent as X-Auth-Token. App-level OAuth (authorization code) is used for apps registered in the Developer Portal; draft apps can be installed on your own stores. Account-level tokens also exist.
access_notes: A free BigCommerce trial/sandbox store gives API credentials via Settings > API Accounts. You don't need to be a partner to build and test an app; partnership is needed only to submit to the App Marketplace.
blocker_notes: Marketplace publishing needs an approved Technology Partner account, but that is not required to build and test a toolkit.

evidence.quote: BigCommerce supports MCP in three ways.
Agents connect to `https://api.bigcommerce.com/mcp`, sign in through the standard BigCommerce login (OAuth 2.1 with PKCE), and then the user chooses which store to connect.
Sign up for a free BigCommerce trial store to test API calls and build integrations without affecting live data.
Navigate to **Settings > API Accounts** in your store control panel. Create credentials with the scopes you need.
You don’t need to be a partner to build and test an app. You can test in any BigCommerce store.
For everything else, use the [REST and GraphQL APIs](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference).
